newsitem.title: CROATIA: Bosnian Croats and Moslems agree on Mostar police.
newsitem.headline: Bosnian Croats and Moslems agree on Mostar police.

text.p: The presidents of Croatia and Bosnia may meet next week after Bosnian Croats and Moslems in the divided city of Mostar agreed to establish a joint police force, a Croatian foreign ministry source said on Friday.
The meeting between Croatia's Franjo Tudjman and Bosnia's Alija Izetbegovic has been postponed several times since April as the two sides manoeuvred for better starting positions.
Bosnian Croats and Moslems fought for control of Mostar in 1994 during the Bosnian war and it has remained divided between the two communities.
Western diplomats regard the integration of their separate and hostile police forces as necessary to end partition.

The agreement on Thursday envisages a new force with a unified command structure and a single uniform, under one ministry. Officers would patrol together, and the uniform and insignia are due to be introduced by August 1.
Tudjman, as patron of the Bosnian Croats, has come under increasing pressure from Washington to make good on commitments he made under the 1995 Dayton peace agreement which included Mostar.
The recent history of Moslem-Croat relations is littered with accords that have not been honoured.
